subtitle: Dara Shukoh and the Secret Fire of the Upanishads

panels.shot: low-angle, half-length portrait against a faint double backdrop of a mosque dome and a temple shikhara
panels.action: Dara Shukoh stands in princely robes, one hand on a closed Persian manuscript and the other resting on a palm-leaf bundle, his gaze steady, as faint outlines of Banaras ghats and Agra’s marble rise behind him.

dialogue.text: In the waning light of Shah Jahan’s court, Prince Dara Shukoh opened hidden Sanskrit books, seeking a single truth in the tongues of Sufis and seers.

i18n.hi: शाहजहाँ की ढलती अदालत में, शहज़ादा दारा शिकोह ने छुपी संस्कृत किताबें खोलीं, सूफियों और ऋषियों की ज़बान में एक ही सच तलाशते हुए।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a balcony overlooking the Yamuna at Agra Fort
panels.action: On an Agra Fort balcony, Dara Shukoh leans over a low desk scattered with Persian papers, while the marble domes of Shah Jahan’s palaces glow in the late afternoon haze beyond the Yamuna.

dialogue.text: The Mughal empire glittered in marble and silk, yet its princes lived in shadows of war, ambition and whispered verses about the soul.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल सल्तनत संगमरमर और रेशम में चमकती थी, पर उसके शहज़ादे जंग, लालच और रूह पर फुसफुसाती कविताओं की छाया में जीते थे।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Dara in his study, lamplight and darkness around
panels.action: In a lamplit chamber lined with shelves of Persian and Arabic books, Dara Shukoh sits cross-legged, tracing lines in a manuscript of Ibn Arabi, his brow furrowed in absorbed thought.

dialogue.text: Dara, eldest son of Shah Jahan, walked the inner paths of the Sufis, reading by oil lamp while cannons and courtiers prepared for succession.

i18n.hi: शाहजहाँ का सबसे बड़ा बेटा दारा, सूफियों के अंदरूनी रास्तों पर चलता, दीये की रोशनी में पढ़ता, जब तोपें और दरबारी गद्दी की जंग की तैयारी करते।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Dara writing at a low desk
panels.action: Over his shoulder we see Dara writing in elegant Persian on a long sheet, a clean margin titled in bold calligraphy, while beside him lie a few Sanskrit-looking palm leaves and notes.

dialogue.text: By 1655 he set his thoughts in ink as Majma al-Bahrain, The Mingling of Two Oceans, matching Sufi words with Vedantic echoes he had begun to hear.

i18n.hi: १६५५ तक उसने अपनी सोच को स्याही में उतारा— मजमा-उल-बहरीन, दो समुद्रों का मिलन, जहाँ सूफी शब्दों को उसने सुनती हुई वेदांतिक गूँजों से जोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of a Mughal hall, small scholarly gathering at center
panels.action: In a modest but elegant Mughal hall in Agra, Dara Shukoh sits on a carpet facing a circle of bearded Muslim scholars and a few Brahmin pandits in simple dhotis, all seated respectfully before him.

dialogue.text: He asked questions that unsettled neat borders: what if the Sufi’s ‘haqiqat’ and the rishi’s ‘tattva’ pointed toward the same sea?

i18n.hi: वो ऐसे सवाल पूछता जो खाँचों को हिला दें: अगर सूफ़ी की ‘हक़ीक़त’ और ऋषि का ‘तत्त्व’ एक ही समंदर की ओर इशारा करें तो?

panels.shot: medium shot, profile view, Dara listening intensely
panels.action: In profile, Dara Shukoh listens intently as an unseen pandit gestures beyond the frame; his hand rests gently on a rolled-up palm-leaf manuscript, his face a mix of curiosity and resolve.

dialogue.speaker: dara_shukoh
dialogue.text: If these are the secret roots, bring me the tree itself.

i18n.hi: अगर ये जड़ें हैं, तो मुझे पूरा पेड़ दिखाओ।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of Banaras ghats on the Ganga
panels.action: From above, dawn mist curls over the crowded ghats of Banaras, priests and pilgrims moving like small figures along the Ganga as a Mughal boat with a small royal canopy approaches the stone steps.

dialogue.text: His search drew him to Banaras, where smoke, bells and Sanskrit chants rose over the Ganga, and where the Upanishads were guarded on brittle leaves.

i18n.hi: उसकी तलाश उसे बनारस ले आई, जहाँ धुआँ, घंटियाँ और संस्कृत मंत्र गंगा के ऊपर उठते, और उपनिषद नाज़ुक पत्तों पर छुपाए जाते थे।

panels.shot: medium-wide shot in a Banaras scholar’s courtyard
panels.action: In a shaded Banaras courtyard, lined with low mud walls and a small shrine, Dara sits opposite an elderly Sanskrit pandit, both on woven mats, with bundles of palm-leaf manuscripts stacked between them.

dialogue.text: There he sat on coarse mats, a prince among scrolls, persuading pandits to unroll texts recited in whisper and guarded as sacred inheritance.

i18n.hi: वहाँ वो खुरदुरी चटाइयों पर बैठा, पर्णों के बीच एक शहज़ादा, पंडितों को मनाता कि वो वो ग्रंथ खोलें जिन्हें फुसफुसा कर पढ़ा जाता और विरासत की तरह संभाला जाता था।

panels.action: A close view of Dara’s jeweled hand reaching humbly to receive a tied bundle of palm leaves from the veined hand of the pandit, the rough cord imprinted on the scholar’s fingers.

dialogue.speaker: dara_shukoh
dialogue.text: Let these words walk in Persian, so more ears may hear.

i18n.hi: इन शब्दों को फ़ारसी में चलने दो, ताकि ज़्यादा कान इन्हें सुन सकें।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a temporary Banaras study, low table crowded with texts
panels.action: In a spare room with lime-washed walls in Banaras, Dara Shukoh sits at a low wooden table laden with palm leaves and paper, while two pandits to his side recite from a leaf, fingers marking lines.

dialogue.text: He gathered Sanskrit scholars beside him, their tongues shaping the Upanishads’ dense forests of sound into phrases he could carry into Persian.

i18n.hi: उसने संस्कृत विद्वानों को अपने पास बिठाया, उनकी ज़बानें उपनिषदों के गाढ़े शब्द-जंगल को ऐसे वाक्यों में ढालतीं जिन्हें वो फ़ारसी में उठा सके।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up of text, two scripts visible
panels.action: Over Dara’s shoulder we see a palm leaf etched with Devanagari on one side and, beside it, his fresh Persian lines flowing in black ink across a cream sheet, both anchored by a simple stone paperweight.

dialogue.text: Syllable by syllable they moved verses about the Self and the Absolute into another script, carrying meaning more than perfect word for word.

i18n.hi: वो अक्षर-अक्षर आत्मा और परम सत्य पर श्लोकों को दूसरी लिपि में ले गए, मतलब बचाते हुए, बिना हर शब्द को जस का तस पकड़ने की ज़िद के।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Dara’s face, lit by lamp
panels.action: In tight close-up, the warm glow of a small lamp lights Dara’s concentrated face as he pauses mid-sentence, lips moving silently as if testing the taste of a Sanskrit phrase he has just heard.

dialogue.speaker: dara_shukoh
dialogue.text: Atman… ruh… is this the same breath under different names?

i18n.hi: आत्मन… रूह… क्या ये एक ही साँस है, बस नाम अलग हैं?

panels.shot: wide shot of a Delhi library room, multiple scribes working
panels.action: In a large library room in Delhi, scribes sit in rows copying clean Persian text from Dara’s master manuscript, while he stands at the back with a pandit, checking a line against a palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Back in imperial cities, he turned these slow labours into a project of empire, supervising copies as if mustering troops of ink.

i18n.hi: फिर शाही शहरों में लौटकर, उसने इन धीमे कामों को सल्तनती मिशन बना दिया, नक़लों की निगरानी करता जैसे स्याही की फ़ौज उतार रहा हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dara presenting a manuscript in a Mughal audience hall
panels.action: Within a Mughal audience hall, its walls painted with floral designs, Dara kneels forward, offering a bound Persian manuscript to an older court scholar seated near a carved pillar.

dialogue.text: He called the work Sirr-i-Akbar, The Great Secret, convinced that the Upanishads contained the earliest revelation hinted at by mystics of his own path.

i18n.hi: उसने इस काम का नाम रखा सिर्र-ए-अकबर, महान रहस्य, यक़ीन था कि उपनिषदों में वही पहली वह़ी छिपी है जिसकी झलक उसके सूफी बुज़ुर्गों ने दी थी।

panels.shot: low-angle shot showing Dara in the foreground, distant silhouette of Aurangzeb in background corridor
panels.action: From a low angle, Dara stands in the foreground with a manuscript under his arm, while far behind him in a shadowed corridor, the distant figure of Aurangzeb walks flanked by soldiers.

dialogue.text: Yet the palace was not only ink and questions. His brother Aurangzeb gathered jurists and troops, and some whispered that Dara’s books bent the law too far.

i18n.hi: पर महल सिर्फ स्याही और सवालों से नहीं भरा था। उसका भाई औरंगज़ेब फक़ीहों और फ़ौजें जुटा रहा था, और कुछ कहते कि दारा की किताबें शरीअत को बहुत दूर तक मोड़ देती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot, Dara in a simple room, faint sounds of distant commotion outside
panels.action: In a plain chamber, Dara Shukoh sits again with a pandit and a Muslim scholar, palms and paper before them, while through an open lattice faintly we see soldiers rushing in a courtyard beyond.

dialogue.text: Even as war clouds gathered, he kept turning pages, sure that arguments about his faith and loyalty were knotted into the struggle for the throne.

i18n.hi: जंग के बादल घिरते रहे, फिर भी वो पन्ने पलटता रहा, यकीन था कि उसके ईमान और वफ़ादारी के झगड़े, तख़्त की लड़ाई से ही बंधे हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of the colophon page being written
panels.action: A scribe’s hand carefully inscribes a neat Persian colophon on the final page, while Dara’s ringed finger points to the date and title, his shadow falling across the paper.

dialogue.text: On 8 July 1657 the colophon named the work complete, its fifty-two Upanishads captured in Persian letters and sealed with his princely ambition.

i18n.hi: ८ जुलाई १६५७ को कोलophon ने लिखा कि काम पूरा हुआ, बावन उपनिषद फ़ारसी अक्षरों में क़ैद थे, उसके शहज़ादगी के सपने की मुहर के साथ।

panels.shot: wide shot of a chest of manuscripts being closed
panels.action: In a dim storeroom, Dara oversees attendants carefully placing several bound Persian volumes and palm-leaf bundles into a wooden chest, which an older librarian gently closes.

dialogue.text: Soon battle and trial would end his life, his defeat written in chains and decrees, but the books themselves slipped quietly into libraries and private chests.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही जंग और मुक़दमे ने उसकी ज़िंदगी खत्म कर दी, उसकी हार ज़ंजीरों और फ़रमानों में लिखी गई, पर किताबें खुद चुपचाप किताबख़ानों और निजी संदूकों में घुस गईं।

panels.shot: soft focus still life of an old Persian codex open beside palm-leaf manuscripts
panels.action: On an aged wooden table, an old Persian codex of Sirr-i-Akbar lies open beside stacked palm-leaf manuscripts, a faint beam of light falling across the two contrasting scripts.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars in distant cities still turn those pages, tracing how Dara’s attempt to bind Sufi and Vedantic insight let ideas travel where his body could not.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद दूर शहरों के विद्वान अब भी वही पन्ने पलटते, देखते हैं कैसे दारा की कोशिश, सूफी और वेदांतिक नूर को बाँधने की, ख़्यालों को वहाँ तक ले गई जहाँ उसका बदन कभी नहीं पहुँच सका।

title_i18n.en: The Prince Who Read the Hidden Books

subtitle_i18n.en: Dara Shukoh and the Secret Fire of the Upanishads
subtitle_i18n.hi: दारा शिकोह और उपनिषदों की गुप्त ज्वाला
